report.source_text: The histopathologic pictureshowed a variable epithelial, neuroendocrine–neuroectodermal and mesenchymal differentiation pattern. The epithelial component included both squamoid (mostly fetal type or immature) cells with clear cytoplasm. These areas were positive by immunohistochemistry for AE1/3, CK7, MNF116, P63 and CDX2. The neuroendocrine–neuroectodermal component was synaptophysin, chromogranin, AE1/3, MNF116, CD56, calretinin and S100 positive, and the nuclei had the typical salt-and-pepper type of chromatin pattern. The mesenchymal component consisted of hypercellular areas of spindle cells with increased mitoses without a specific type of differentiation (such as skeletal muscle, cartilage, fat, etc). These areas were positive for androgen receptor and desmin, and SOX10 and myogenin were negative.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his 50s presented to the emergency department with difficulty breathing through the nose. Imaging studies, including CT and MRI, revealed a sizeable soft tissue mass in the nasopharynx, measuring 1.6x6.3x4.6 cm3, extending into the ostiomeatal complex, left frontal recess, sphenoethmoidal recess, and pterygopalatine fossa. He underwent a complex surgical resection of the tumor, involving an ipsilateral medial maxillectomy, total ethmoidectomy, septectomy, and anterior skull base resection via an endonasal approach. Histopathological examination of the resected tissue showed a variable epithelial, neuroendocrine–neuroectodermal, and mesenchymal differentiation pattern with specific immunohistochemical findings, which were consistent with the diagnosis of Sinonasal Teratocarcinosarcoma (SNTCS), also referred to as malignant teratoma.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with difficulty breathing through the nose.

CT and MRI scans revealed a sizeable soft tissue mass in the nasopharynx, measuring 1.6x6.3x4.6 cm3, arising from the medial wall of the lateral wall of the nose and extending into the ostiomeatal complex, the left frontal recess and the sphenoethmoidal recess, with associated fullness and expansion of the pterygopalatine fossa.
A complex surgical resection of the tumor was performed, including an ipsilateral medial maxillectomy, total ethmoidectomy, septectomy, and anterior skull base resection, via an endonasal approach.

Histopathological examination of the resected tissue showed a variable epithelial, neuroendocrine–neuroectodermal and mesenchymal differentiation pattern with specific immunohistochemical findings (positive for AE1/3, CK7, MNF116, P63, CDX2 in epithelial component; synaptophysin, chromogranin, AE1/3, MNF116, CD56, calretinin, S100 in neuroendocrine–neuroectodermal component; androgen receptor and desmin in mesenchymal component).
The overall findings from histopathology were consistent with the diagnosis of SNTCS, also referred to as malignant teratoma.
